name: MEX Replacement on Tree
description: You are given a tree rooted at $$$1$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices and a permutation $$$p$$$ of length $$$n$$$ consisting of integers $$$0, 1, \ldots, n - 1$$$, where $$$p_v$$$ represents the weight of vertex $$$v$$$. Let $$$S_v$$$ denote the set of weights written on the vertices belonging to the path from $$$1$$$ to $$$v$$$. Define a function $$$f$$$ as $$$f(v) = \mathrm{MEX}(S_v)$$$, that is, the $$$\mathrm{MEX}$$$ over the set consisting of the weights of vertices on the simple path between the root and $$$v$$$ (inclusive), where $$$\operatorname{MEX}$$$ of a collection of integers $$$c_1, c_2, \ldots, c_k$$$ is defined as the smallest non-negative integer $$$x$$$ which does not occur in the collection $$$c$$$. Also, given the following operation: Choose an integer $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq v \leq n$$$) and assign $$$f(v)$$$ to $$$p_v$$$. Your goal is to find the maximum value of $$$\sum\limits_{v = 1}^n f(v)$$$ after performing the above operation no more than once (possibly zero).
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 2 \cdot 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of vertices of the tree. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$$$ ($$$0 \le p_i \le n - 1$$$) — the elements of array $$$p$$$. It is guaranteed that every integer from $$$0$$$ to $$$n - 1$$$ appears exactly once in $$$p$$$. Then $$$n - 1$$$ lines follow, each line contains two integers $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$ ($$$1 \le x_i, y_i \le n$$$), indicating an edge between vertices $$$x_i$$$ and $$$y_i$$$. It is guaranteed that these edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single line containing an integer: the maximum value of $$$\sum\limits_{v = 1}^n f(v)$$$ after performing the above operation no more than once (possibly zero).
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2219D — MEX Replacement on Tree [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
